q1_connect_resends_first.answer: No. aud_connector_connect (0x6006f600) and aud_module_connect (0x60074154) never touch out_port->current_first (+0x140) and send no event. aud_module_connect only sets in_port->up_peer (+0xec, s32i at 0x6007416d) under async_up_lock and appends in_port to out_port->down_peer_root (aud_link_add_tail 0x6007417f). Nothing — neither the stored first nor a dummy — is sent at connect time. The output port is reused if it already exists (aud_module_new_output loop 0x60073cb2..0x60073cc1 -> 0x60073cea), so its current_first survives a re-route; the new input port is calloc-like zeroed (0x158 bytes, 0x60073be8) so in_port->current_first starts NULL. The first-event hand-over is deferred to the first data chain (see q2).

q2_pending_first_replay.answer: Neither foreach_down_peer_push_data (0x60072694) nor aud_port_push_event (0x600727a4) contains replay logic; neither reads +0x140. The replay is in aud_module_chain_locked (0x600746d4), called by foreach_down_peer_push_data at 0x60072788 for each down-peer. Trigger: peer(input port)->current_first (+0x140) == NULL (0x600747c5/0x600747ca). Then: if peer->up_peer (+0xec) != NULL and up_peer->current_first != NULL -> e = aud_object_get(up_peer->current_first), i.e. THE STORED FIRST EVENT OBJECT ITSELF (refcount++, same object, same key-values) (0x600748b2..0x600748c2); else e = aud_event_new_first() — an empty dummy (type=1, flags DOWNWARD|SYNC, no key-values; 0x60069e20). e is stored in peer->current_first (0x6007490d) and delivered via module->impl->event(module, peer, get(e)) (0x60074910..0x60074920). Separately, on the OUTPUT side, add_pending_obj_locked (0x60072078) fills an empty out_port->current_first when DATA is queued: from module->first_event_out (+0xa8, the module's last INPUT first event) if set, else a dummy aud_event_new_first(); this only sets the stored pointer and does not push any event downstream.

q3_reroute_after_first.answer: Yes, with conditions — but lazily. A new downstream peer connected after the FIRST was already synced receives nothing at connect time; on the first DATA that flows to it, aud_module_chain_locked sees its current_first==NULL and hands it the upstream output port's stored current_first object (same refcounted event, hence the original es/codec/data-rate key-values), via impl->event, before chaining the data. It gets an empty dummy instead if, at that moment, up_peer->current_first is NULL: e.g. after a LAST_AU cleared it (0x60072118..1a), if the output port was newly created by the connect and never carried a FIRST (then add_pending_obj_locked may itself have stored module->first_event_out or a dummy when data was queued — so the peer gets that, which is the module's input-side first, or a value-less dummy), or if the output port was deleted/recreated (e.g. via a module's deleting_port or aud_module_del_output_port).
q3_reroute_after_first.confidence: high for the mechanism; medium for real-world outcome (depends on whether the upstream output port persists and on module impl->event behaviour)
